chapter: The rhythm section, family and records
title: What musicians' families sacrifice
summary: Hinton and Jones talk about the toll of travel on musicians' wives and children and the unseen supports that sustained them.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: They don't know the dues that we put to work and to travel and try to support them and try to lend

some support at home. Sometimes we suffer from it, our wives suffer from it, and our children suffer from it in order to sacrifice and give to the world this little talent that God has given us. This is what you've done, Jo, you've suffered greatly to divide yourself into 4 million pieces to give to the world that which you're so talented with and to provide for your family and being away from your home, because we had to travel the way we had to travel, we take responsibility for some of the leniency and some of the laxness that's happened with our children. So anyway we just want to go into that -

Milt, what we don't delve into, we do not say the Supreme Being, which is a God, or whatever God that anyone - we got 400 different religions out here and cults and what have you. We always chalk it up to - because I didn't know what they meant when I was a kid, on carnivals and circuses at 16 up to... But it's the most gratifying thing that peoples have been nice to our families, see, because when we're not there there's someone they - you know good and well of how you used to go when various ones were born different places and look in on different people's families to see how the food was, how the clothing was, and how was so-and-so.
